description: Bare is a de-Googled Chromium build for Android, built for privacy, control, and freedom on the web. It strips Google tracking, telemetry, and AI integration while keeping browser extensions and uBlock Origin. It adds background video playback, saving media from sites that normally block it, your choice of download manager, and more.

latest_release.name: Bare 2.0.7
latest_release.body:
# Bare 2.0.7

Bare 2.0.7 fixes extension installs, a download crash and the address bar, on top of 2.0.5. It also carries the 2.0.6 fixes, which were not posted as a release of their own. Chromium is unchanged at 157.0.8103.78.

## Which APK to download

For most phones, download `Bare-2.0.7-arm64-v8a.apk`. Use `Bare-2.0.7-armeabi-v7a.apk` only on 32-bit ARM devices. Bare runs on Android 10 or later. There is no x86 build.

There are also two `Bare-crashlab` APKs for finding crashes. You do not need them for normal use. See `docs/crashlab.md` for what they do and what the log can hold. The CrashLab hashes are in `SHA256SUMS-crashlab.txt`.

The log lists the sites you visited and other app messages. Look through it before you send it to anyone.

## Installing and updating

Install over Bare 2.0.0 to 2.0.5 and do not uninstall first. The package name and signing key are the same and the version number is higher, so Android should treat it as an update that keeps your data. You cannot go back to an older version without wiping Bare's data.

The GitHub build checks for updates, so Bare's own update check will offer 2.0.7. The Google Play build does not check for updates.

## What's new

- Adding extensions from the Chrome Web Store, or from a .crx link, works again.
- The address is centered again in the address bar when you are not typing.
- Downloads no longer crash on some Android 16 phones.
- A site name that is too long for the address bar now keeps its start and ends in an ellipsis, instead of losing its first letters.
- The toolbar folds away when you scroll even with TalkBack or another accessibility service on. To keep it on screen, turn on Keep toolbar visible.
- Fixed a crash that could happen with the address bar at the bottom.

## Things to know

- A long site name is cut at the end now, so a very long address can hide its last part, including the real domain, while you are not typing. Tap the bar to see the whole address.
- The crash fixes come from reading the code and from crash reports. We have not seen every case on a phone, so tell us if a crash is still there.

## Versions

- Version name: 2.0.7
- Version codes: 802000715 (arm64), 802000710 (32-bit ARM)
- Chromium: 157.0.8103.78

## Verifying the download

`SHA256SUMS.txt` has the SHA-256 of the two Bare APKs. The CrashLab hashes are in `SHA256SUMS-crashlab.txt`.

```
d18c497243b95eb36de34f37e332d04f54bdeb3e7029f91cad6ac9aa4a203639  Bare-2.0.7-arm64-v8a.apk
19ee3299d41c9ea6bd894997d0b841878c222401208a15d52a71135eff5c1fc4  Bare-2.0.7-armeabi-v7a.apk
```

Both are signed with Bare's release key, the same one as earlier releases. `apksigner verify --print-certs` should show the certificate SHA-256 `ae2a0e7fb7a132ec517d26a8e7c83d275e83747b0a777d4a42225b1d343271a0`.

## Contact

Problems and questions: support@barebrowser.org. Please include your device, Android version and what you were doing.

detail.readme:
Bare Browser

[Website](https://barebrowser.org) · [Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=org.barebrowser) · [Download APK](https://github.com/BareBrowser/bare-browser/releases/latest)
Bare removes Google sign-in, browser telemetry and AI features from Chromium. Desktop extensions work, and uBlock Origin comes installed. - Version: `2.0.7`. versionCode `802000715` (arm64) and `802000710` (32-bit arm). - Base: Chromium `157.0.8103.78` (commit `4b3d0dab`). - Runs on: Android 10 or newer, on arm64 or 32-bit ARM. There is no x86 build. - Size: 346 patches, 79,520 insertions and 4,477 deletions across 1,157 files. ## What you can do - Install desktop extensions from the Chrome Web Store, a CRX file or an unpacked folder. Pin the ones you use to the toolbar. - Use the full [uBlock Origin](https://github.com/gorhill/uBlock), included by default. You can disable or remove it. - Put the address bar at the top or bottom, arrange the toolbar, and switch between list and grid views for tabs. - Open your tabs in a drawer that slides in from the left, as page thumbnails or as a list. The regular tab switcher has the same grid or list choice. - Set each button on the bottom bar, including Find in page, Search, Back, Forward and the tabs drawer. Swipe along the bottom bar or the address bar to switch tabs. A minimal address bar is a single row with New tab, Tabs and Menu, and you can hide items from the three dot menu. - Find Settings grouped into Your Browser, Preferences & tools and Bare. Pick an app icon (Light, Dark or Retro), let the System theme use true black, and make pages fit the phone's width while keeping the user agent you chose. - Manage extensions on a phone-sized page that shows each one's version and status, with switches for Enabled and Allow in Incognito, Install CRX, Load unpacked and Update all. Bare offers to install a `.crx` when it finishes downloading, and the Chrome Web Store is laid out as a phone list. - Translate pages by sending their text to a LibreTranslate-compatible server that you enter, after you confirm. Google Translate is a separate choice and stays off until you turn it on. - Lock Incognito with fingerprint or face only, wipe it after 1, 3 or 5 failed unlocks, and allow or block screenshots in it. - Turn on security options: secure connections, third-party cookie blocking, hiding your local address in WebRTC and hardened JavaScript. - Receive web push through a distributor app that you pick in Settings, instead of through Google. - Keep supported video playing with the screen off. Save media from a page, or send downloads to another manager. The other app gets the page address and the User-Agent, and your cookies only if you allow it, never from Incognito. Long press a video that a page streams and choose Download video to fetch the file the page names. - Choose your search engine. DuckDuckGo is the default; Google (No AI) is available, and you can add your own.


## Install Bare runs on Android 10 or newer, on 64-bit and 32-bit ARM devices. - [Get Bare on Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=org.barebrowser) for updates through Play. - [Download an APK from GitHub](https://github.com/BareBrowser/bare-browser/releases/latest) if you prefer to install it yourself. The release page lists the APK choices, checksums, changes and upgrade notes. ## For developers This repository is a patch series against a pinned Chromium Desktop Android revision. The `patches/` directory holds Bare's changes, numbered in the order they apply; [docs/patches.md](docs/patches.md) says how. To build it yourself, start with [the build guide](docs/build-from-source.md). The [builder notes](BUILDING.md) cover the container, versioning and signing. [Reproducibility](docs/reproducibility.md) explains how to compare a local build with a release, and [build constraints](docs/build-constraints.md) records the upstream limits. ## Network behaviour Bare has no account or telemetry service of its own. It still makes some network requests: Chromium updates security components and may provision Widevine through Google; uBlock Origin fetches filter lists and extension updates. The GitHub APK checks for Bare releases if you enable automatic updates. Google Play handles updates for the Play build. Safe Browsing is unavailable in this build. Bare uses uBlock Origin's malware and phishing lists instead, which block known bad addresses but cover less than Google's lists. See the [measured network behaviour](docs/network-behaviour.md) for the detailed capture and [privacy policy](https://barebrowser.org/privacy) for how browsing data is handled. ## Credits Bare is licensed under [BSD-3-Clause](LICENSE) and built on [Chromium](https://www.chromium.org/). We also look at [Titanium](https://github.com/jqssun/android-titanium-browser), [Cromite](https://github.com/uazo/cromite) and [ungoogled-chromium](https://github.com/ungoogled-software/ungoogled-chromium) when tracing Chromium behaviour. Thanks to the developers who keep that work open. [uBlock Origin](https://github.com/gorhill/uBlock) is by Raymond Hill and contributors. Bare bundles the upstream signed extension without changing its source or repackaging it. It keeps its own GPL-3.0 licence; see [NOTICE](NOTICE). Chromium is a trademark of Google LLC. Bare is independent of Google and the Chromium project.


Made with ❤️ in San Francisco
